quote: Theorem 1. Let Xi ~ M(theta_i), i = 1, 2 be two random variables. If theta_1 <= theta_2, then X1 <lr X2, X1 <hr X2, X1 <s X2 and X1 <cx X2. Proof. We have fX1(t)/fX2(t) = [theta_1^3 (1+theta_2) / theta_2^3 (1+theta_1)] e^{-(theta_1-theta_2)t}. differentiating w.r.t t, we get (d/dt)[fX1(t)/fX2(t)] = -(theta_1 - theta_2) e^{-(theta_1-theta_2)t} < 0, forall theta_1 >= theta_2. Hence, we see that fX1(t)/fX2(t) decreases in t, which holds the above theorem. (proved)
family: Mgamma(theta): finite mixture of Gamma(2, theta) and Gamma(3, theta) with mixing probability theta/(1+theta); pdf f(x) = theta^3 x (1 + x/2) e^{-theta x}/(1+theta), x > 0, theta > 0
compared: two Mgamma variables differing only in the parameter: X1 ~ M(theta_1) vs X2 ~ M(theta_2)

Likelihood Ratio order (X <lr Y), if f_X(t)/f_Y(t) is decreasing in t
hypotheses.formal: X <=_lr Y iff f_X(t)/f_Y(t) is decreasing in t

quantifiers: theta_1 <= theta_2, theta_i > 0; ratio decreasing in t for all t > 0
ambiguity: Internal contradiction: the statement assumes theta_1 <= theta_2, but the proof claims the derivative is negative 'forall theta_1 >= theta_2'. With theta_1 <= theta_2 the printed derivative -(theta_1-theta_2)e^{...} is >= 0, so the displayed inequality < 0 does not hold as printed; the conclusion direction is unclear.

Convex order (X <cx Y) if for all convex functions phi and provided expectation exist, E[phi(X)] <= E[phi(Y)]
hypotheses.formal: X <=_cx Y iff E[phi(X)] <= E[phi(Y)] for all convex phi

hypotheses.formal: equal means makes cx equivalent to st

conclusion.direction: X1 <=_cx X2 (X1 smaller in convex order)

ambiguity: Convex order is asserted even though E[X1] != E[X2] when theta_1 != theta_2 (mean is (2theta+3)/(theta(1+theta))), so the Remark 2 equivalence used elsewhere does not apply; the printed proof only argues the lr part. Also the parameter-condition contradiction from the lr part carries over.
